newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Union threatens strike at S.African airports.
newsitem.headline: Union threatens strike at S.African airports.

text.p: South African aviation technicians and engineers have threatened to strike for more wages early next week, South African Airways (SAA), the airports authority, said on Thursday.

SAA spokeswoman Zelda Schuulabach said disruptions caused by a work-to-rule action by about 3,000 members of the South African Aviation Engineering and Allied Union (SAAEAU) which began on Wednesday were mounting.
"The industrial action is continuing and its effects are escalating.
"(The union) has also said now that if they don't get what they are asking for they will go on to a full-blown strike next week Wednesday where no work will be done," Schuulabach told Reuters.

She said that in Johannesburg, which serves as SAA's technical operations hub, two flights to London and Miami had been delayed for about 15 hours overnight -- leaving hundreds of passengers stranded.

The flights were rescheduled to depart on Thursday afternoon, Schuulabach said, adding that some domestic flights had been cancelled on Thursday as part of the contingency plans to try to alleviate the situation.

SAAEAU has declared a dispute with SAA for its refusal to offer a 25 percent wage rise. Management is offering only a 10 percent wage hike plus a 20 percent productivity bonus which the union has refused, Schuulabach said.
Asked if passenger safety was being compromised in the action she said: "With the work-to-rule action they (workers) are taking longer doing the work and in a way they'll probably be more thorough".
SAAEAU officials were unavailable for comment early on Thursday.
